text:
jia: hey folks — running into a weirdness with the Go sampleapp generator + streaming where an auth refresh in the middle of a stream leaves the generator stuck (goroutine leak) instead of surfacing an error we can retry against. repro below, any quick ideas? cc @matt @omar

jia: repro steps: 1) start sampleapp streaming gen with short-lived token 2) wait for token to rotate (we simulate via local KMS) 3) auth refresh triggers 401 from runtime during mid-stream 4) app sees no error on generator.Next(), goroutine stays blocked forever

jia: minimal snippet:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), time.Minute)
defer cancel()
g := client.NewGenerator(cfg)
stream := g.Generate(ctx, opts)
for stream.Next() {
  token := stream.Token() // user-level token header being sent
  fmt.Println(string(stream.Current()))
}
if err := stream.Err(); err != nil {
  log.Printf("stream ended: %v", err)
}
```

matt: hmm, do you see a 401 in the runtime logs or is the connection just dropping?

jia: runtime logs show 401 and then a keep-alive but our side still stuck inside an internal read waiting on frames. No explicit error returned to the user stream object.

omar: yeah this smells like handshake vs mid-stream auth handling in the transport. If we only close the net.Conn without bubbling a concrete error, the generator iterator can block on the receive loop.

omar: quick thought: we should treat a 401 mid-stream as a distinct ErrAuthRefresh (or similar sentinel) that's surfaced by stream.Err(), so callers can decide to refresh token + retry. Right now the transport tries to be "transparent" and that hides the failure.

megan: agreed. Also we hit an ergonomics issue — callers expect generator.Next() to either return false w/ Err() non-nil or allow context cancel. Getting stuck is the worst.

matt: is the auth refresh happening via the SDK's token provider callback? If so maybe we need to pause send/recv while token rotates and then retry handshake for that stream id instead of letting TCP linger. That would keep the generator semantics intact.

jia: token provider does background refresh and updates header supplier. But by the time runtime rejects a request mid-stream, the transport code just tries to read, doesn't escalate the auth error up the iterator.

omar: I'll prototype a patch: 1) detect 401 frames in stream control path 2) close the recv loop with a sentinel error "errAuthRefresh" 3) expose generator.IsRetryable(err) helper AND export the sentinel so sampleapps can pattern-match.

megan: prefer err name like ErrStreamAuthRefresh or ErrAuthRefreshRequired — explicit. Add docs example showing pattern:
```go
for g.Next() { ... }
if errors.Is(g.Err(), redwood.ErrStreamAuthRefresh) {
  // get new token and recreate generator or call client.RetryStream(...)
}
```

jia: sounds good. downside: callers must re-create stream; can we add a helper on client to reattach/resume? That would be nicer for onboarding sampleapps.

omar: resume semantics are tricky because generator state (KV cache, partial outputs) isn't trivially reconstructable. I think re-create is safer initially. We can add a higher-level helper later.

matt: one more UX nit — when we return ErrStreamAuthRefresh, we should surface the raw status and maybe a suggestedRetryAfter header if runtime provided it. Saves guesswork in sampleapps.

ci-bot: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/actions failed: TestGeneratorStreamAuthRefresh (see CI job 8421)

megan: thanks CI. @omar can you link that failing test in the PR? Also add an integration test that simulates token rotation mid-stream to prevent regressions.

omar: yup will do. I'll open a draft PR with tests + exported ErrStreamAuthRefresh and a small sampleapp patch that demonstrates retry flow.

jia: awesome — once PR lands I can update our onboarding sample to show the pattern and avoid the leak. also file a docs note under "streaming auth" so users know what to do on 401 mid-stream.

matt: thanks team. low-priority follow-up: consider a convenience client.RetryableGenerate(ctx, opts, tokenRefresher) in a subsequent iteration for better DX.

megan: agreed. For now, prioritize crash/unstuck fix + tests + sampleapp update.

jia: I'll add a short issue for the sampleapp doc and link PR when ready. thanks!
